mizu 水 

  ________
 /\       \
/  \  mizu \
\  /   水  /
 \/_______/

mizu uses shared memory to make communication between R processes fast enough to parallelize work at thread granularity.

Task round trips drop from around 100 µs over sockets to under a microsecond — two orders of magnitude (see Benchmarks). The hot path never enters the kernel and data is never copied through a system socket.

Channels and work-stealing task pools run over POSIX shared memory (Linux, macOS) or Win32 file mappings (Windows): lock-free single-producer single-consumer rings with batched publication, spin-then-park waiting, and peer death delivered as an OS event.

mizu is built on libmizu, a C library for lock-free shared-memory IPC. pymizu binds the same core for Python, so R and Python can talk to each other.

  • Zero-copy vectors and data frames — received as ALTREP views over the shared pages
  • Zero-copy Arrow interchange — arrow tables and record batches travel as one frame, converting back without copying
  • Event-driven async — messages stream into a later event loop without polling, and channels, tasks, and maps plug into promises pipelines, ready for Shiny
  • Reproducible parallel random numbers (.seed) — identical results for any worker count or steal order
  • Nested parallel maps — a task can map over its own pool, deadlock-free

Pre-release. The API is not stable and can change at any time before a release.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

pak::pak("shikokuchuo/mizu")

Requires R 4.3 or later on a 64-bit platform (Linux: kernel 5.3 or later).

Quickstart 

library(mizu)

p <- mizu_pool(n_workers = 4L)

t <- mizu_submit(p, sum(x) + y, x = 1:10, y = 100)
mizu_collect(t)
#> [1] 155

mizu_pool_stop(p)

Benchmarks

Communication overhead against mirai on one machine (M4 Pro, from dev/bench/mizu-mirai-bench.R):

Benchmark mizu mirai Speedup
Trivial task round trip 0.8 µs 100.5 µs 126x
Pipelined throughput, 1 worker 833,000 tasks/s 9,700 tasks/s 86x
8 MB vector round trip 400 µs 18.4 ms 46x
Parallel map of 2,000 ~10 µs tasks, 4 workers 5.0 ms 218 ms 44x

Note: mirai also serves workers on remote machines and HPC clusters, which shared memory cannot reach.

Parallel map

mizu_map() maps a function over a vector or list on the pool and returns a map handle immediately, like mizu_submit() returns a task. mizu_collect() on the handle waits and returns the results in order; as.promise() (or then() directly) collects through the event loop instead. The function and data cross into shared memory once. Workers divide the elements among themselves, claiming ranges from a shared cursor.

A map also nests — the mapped function can map over its own pool with mizu_map(mizu_current_pool(), ...), deadlock-free.

p <- mizu_pool(n_workers = 4L)

m <- mizu_map(p, 1:5, \(i) i * 2L, .template = integer(1))
mizu_collect(m)
#> [1]  2  4  6  8 10

parts <- split(as.numeric(1:100000), rep(1:4, each = 25000))
m <- mizu_map(p, parts, \(part) {
  nested <- mizu_map(mizu_current_pool(), part, sqrt, .template = numeric(1))
  sum(mizu_collect(nested))
}, .template = numeric(1))
mizu_collect(m)
#>       1       2       3       4 
#> 2635310 4818361 6239529 7388808

mizu_pool_stop(p)

Python interop

Pool workers can be Python processes that run pymizu, the Python binding of the same core. mizu_py_launcher() spawns them and mizu_call() describes the task — here R’s built-in mtcars summarized by polars:

p <- mizu_pool(n_workers = 4L, launcher = mizu_py_launcher())

t <- mizu_submit_call(
  p,
  mizu_call(
    .source = r"(import polars as pl
pl.DataFrame(x).group_by('cyl').agg(pl.col('mpg').mean()).sort('cyl'))",
    x = mtcars
  )
)
mizu_collect(t)
#>   cyl      mpg
#> 1   4 26.66364
#> 2   6 19.74286
#> 3   8 15.10000

mizu_pool_stop(p)
  • A numeric vector arrives in Python as a NumPy array, and a data frame as a pymizu.Frame
  • A NumPy array, or a polars, pyarrow, or pandas frame, arrives back as a vector or data frame
  • Arrow data (arrow tables and record batches, or any struct-typed nanoarrow_array_stream) crosses the same way

The pymizu README shows the reverse direction: a Python host that drives R workers with pymizu.r_launcher().

Vignettes

vignette("mizu", package = "mizu") is the main overview. Topic vignettes cover benchmarks against mirai, channels, task pools, the parallel map, Python interop, and operations (sizing /dev/shm on Linux, tuning the Linux memory allocator, and crash semantics). The pkgdown site has the function reference and the rendered vignettes.
